case_title: Uttam Chakraborty v. State of Assam
accused_occupation: Mission Suklabaidhya (first accused): retired Army personnel. Uttam Chakraborty (second accused): Not stated
accused_victim_relationship: Spouse (first accused was the victim's husband). Second accused was a friend of the husband, with no relationship to the victim described (Acquaintance).
weapon: Kerosene oil (fire/burns), as stated in the FIR; no other weapon described
evidence_type: Eyewitness (child witness PW-6); retracted section 164 CrPC statement of PW-1; medical (post-mortem and inquest); motive evidence from victim's mother; circumstantial (presence at scene)
aggravating_circumstances: Crime described as truly horrendous; murder committed in the matrimonial house; victim was about eight months pregnant and the foetus had been removed
trial_court_outcome: Both convicted under s.302 IPC; first accused sentenced to death; second accused sentenced to life imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Death reference confirmed; accused's appeal dismissed, convictions and sentences upheld
offence_finally_established: Murder (IPC s.302) against the first accused (Mission Suklabaidhya). The second accused's conviction was set aside.
neutral_facts: On a night in April 2004, the victim, who was about eight months pregnant, was found dead from burn injuries in the matrimonial home. The victim's household included the accused, a young child of about four or five years, and a domestic helper of about sixteen years. The victim had reportedly discovered an illicit relationship between the first accused and the domestic helper, and the couple had frequent quarrels. Around 2 a.m., a local resident and several others came to the victim's mother's house, told her the victim was ill, and took her to the police station. There she found the first accused and the domestic helper, who told her the victim had died of burn injuries. The mother lodged a first information report around 2.30 a.m., stating that she had learnt the victim died in a fire caused by kerosene oil, and alleging the victim had been killed by her husband. A shop-owner stated that around 10 to 10.30 p.m. he saw two men in an animated discussion, and that a girl came out shouting that the wife had died of burn injuries. The child witness identified the accused in court. The domestic helper had named both accused in a statement before a magistrate, but did not support that statement at trial. The victim's mother deposed to the illicit relationship. The executive magistrate who held the inquest noted a large cut injury on the body. The doctor who conducted the post-mortem found very severe cut injuries to the stomach indicating that the foetus had been removed.
physical_harm: Death from burn injuries; very severe cut injuries to the abdomen indicating removal of an eight-month foetus
number_of_offences: 1 charged (IPC s.302); 1 finally upheld (first accused only; second accused's conviction set aside)
motive: Accepted by the courts below as corroborated: the first accused's illicit relationship with the domestic helper, which the victim objected to, causing frequent quarrels
key_evidence_accepted: Child witness PW-6's testimony (credibility not doubted, but not a safe basis for a death sentence); PW-5's corroboration of motive; post-mortem findings of PW-7; murder in matrimonial house
witness_credibility: PW-6 credibility not doubted. PW-1 resiled from her section 164 statement at trial. PW-4's evidence cannot connect the second accused. PW-6 apparently mistook the second accused for PW-4.
trial_duration: offence: 13/14 April 2004; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 26.04.2006; Supreme Court: April 6, 2010
legal_representation: Appellants: S.B. Sanyal, Azim H. Laskar, Sachiri Das (printed as 'Oas'), Rana Mukherjee, Abhijit Sengupta. State (respondent): J.R. Luwang, Navneert (for Corporate Law Group).
investigation_status: FIR lodged around 2.30 a.m.; section 164 CrPC statement of PW-1 recorded; investigation completed; charged with murder; tried
appeal_history: Trial court: both convicted under s.302; first accused death, second life. High Court: death reference confirmed, appeal dismissed. Supreme Court: first accused's appeal (871/2006) dismissed as to conviction, sentence commuted to life; second accused's appeal (869/2006) allowed, conviction and sentence set aside.
legal_principle_applied: A section 164 CrPC statement is not substantive evidence; the court must examine other evidence given in court. Child witness evidence is not a safe basis for a capital sentence. A conviction requires evidence connecting the accused with the offence.
precedent_relied_upon: Suresh v. State of U.P. (1981) 2 SCC 569; Raja Ram Yadav & Ors. v. State of Bihar (1996) 9 SCC 287
sentencing_rationale: Although the child witness's credibility was not doubted, a capital sentence would be imprudent when based on a child witness's statement, so the death sentence was commuted to life imprisonment
judicial_aggravating_factors: Crime described by the Court as truly horrendous
other_sentence_order: Second accused directed to be set free forthwith, if not wanted in any other case
